sonnet.problem: The wrong answer "He makes a lame man walk at the synagogue" is close to the right answer. Making a lame man walk is a healing of a sick person, so a baker could argue it fits "lay His hands on a few of the sick and heal them" (Mark 6:5). The text doesn't rule out which sick people He healed, so this wrong answer could be argued as right.
sonnet.rule: **No near-matches.** A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
